method: First reasoned review: atomscan and cleave facts (including decoded text) for every supplied sample; pefile/Capstone native disassembly, rizin cross-check of the x86 injection routine, dnfile/dncil full CIL method decoding and token resolution, and Go objdump. No sample was executed. ML labels, scores, strings and prior repository reviews were not used as behavior proof.
external_sources: The three supplied tria.ge pages were inaccessible through the web tool. No external-source behavior claims were imported.
changes: Remove confuserex-managed-http-dropper-hidden-launch: unrelated HTTP response, file-write and hidden-process API references neither bind a payload to execution nor establish ConfuserEx. Keep all individual notable capability findings; no package exceptions or severity demotions.

Add suspicious managed-dual-debugger-check-exit-layout in objectives/anti-analysis/debugger-detect/check: require the short-circuit CIL conditional-call layout, CLR metadata, native and managed debugger references, and Exit member inside .text. Method RIDs, local slots, filenames and endpoints are not fixed. The matcher supports probable gating, not arbitrary CIL token resolution.
No new generic instruction-directory child or size-budget exception: the sequence catalog already contains 100 rules. The atomic YARA condition expresses the full anti-analysis observation together.

reference_audit.retired_rule: No exact-ID YAML consumers. Its constituents remain canonical capability findings.
reference_audit.new_rule: Ancestor consumers in anti-static binary-metrics/profile/hostile.yaml, evasion/process/injection/toolkit/traits.yaml and evasion/masquerade/extension-mismatch/source-code.yaml legitimately select debugger-detection evidence. Their independent required evidence does not hold here; rescan checks for unintended changes.

samples.identification: Modified XMRig-derived x64 self-replicator carrying an appended Go downloader and Cobalt Strike Beacon DLL
samples.marker_line: XMRig-derived self-replicator with Beacon: no change
execution_evidence: Entry 0x14009a338 transfers through CRT 0x14009a1bc; call 0x14009a2c3 enters 0x14002add4. This main opens argv[0], measures and reads its complete bytes through fopen/fseek/ftell/fread at 0x14002ae8c..0x14002aed6.

At 0x14002aee5..0x14002aef5 it reads the last two DWORDs and decrements the first. At 0x14002af15..0x14002afa7 it makes random EXE names in C:/Windows/System/, copies its own image with rewritten trailer, and writes two control DWORDs. CreateProcessW at 0x14002b01d launches each copy; 0x14002b023..0x14002b03e increments the counter and 0xfd padding stride and loops to the footer-specified count. This is unsolicited clone proliferation, distinct from ordinary mining.

The actual final DWORDs are 779505775 and 1583708261 (little endian). They are large positive values, so the clone-loop gates pass. Write permissions, failed file opens and later resource exhaustion can prevent completion; no runtime success is asserted.
Ordinary XMRig pool configuration, Stratum, CPU backends and donation settings remain notable identity/capability evidence. Mining or donation suppression alone does not establish cryptojacking.

Appended x86 Go PE begins at file 0xfc400. main.main calls checkForAdmin (opens PHYSICALDRIVE0), requests runAs via PowerShell on the non-admin branch, and uses TEMP/GData.txt as an existence guard. GetArchive links net/http.Get to io.Copy into a created ZIP; Extract traverses archive/zip members, then main launches C:/G DATA Security Software/AVK.exe. The embedded URL targets an S3 ZIP. No remote content was fetched and no hostile behavior is inferred from its chosen names or endpoint alone.

An independent x86 DLL starts at file 0x5b8601. In that DLL, 0x10009643 XOR-decodes the 4096-byte settings table at 0x10031028 using 0x69; 0x10009660 onward parses typed records. Decoded settings include a 5000 ms sleep, port 443, ns7/ns8/ns9.softline.top endpoints, HTTP profile transformations and rundll32 spawn paths. These are observed configuration, not contacted infrastructure.

DLL DNS queries at 0x10003598 and 0x10003636 call thunk 0x100244c2 -> DNSAPI!DnsQuery_A with TXT and AAAA types and retry handling. Reflective loader code walks loaded modules/exports with ROR13 hashing. This verifies an operative Beacon implementation rather than a name or imported API alone. The outer-to-DLL activation link was not established; embedded capability is not a claim that the outer launches Beacon.
samples.trait_decision: Existing self-replication objective plus embedded Beacon identity/config traits supply multiple independently verified hostile findings. No further behavior rule is needed for this sample.

samples.identification: Damaged StormAttack-style x86 resource DLL injection and shell-cleanup loader
samples.marker_line: Damaged StormAttack DLL injector: no change
execution_evidence: Entry 0x402674 reaches dispatcher 0x401cb0. DWORD at file 0x4120 is 3; 0x401f75..0x401f8f selects self-copy/registry routine 0x401900 followed by cleanup 0x401390.

Routine 0x401900 builds a GUID-like EXE path, writes a registry value, reads the current executable, patches bytes, writes a copy via fwrite at 0x401b26 and calls CreateProcessA at 0x401b7e. The intended Active Setup subkey/value strings are randomized in these bytes, so functioning Active Setup persistence is NOT supported. The current scan correctly does not report it.

Cleanup 0x401390 obtains its own module path, converts it to a short path, reads COMSPEC, constructs /c del <self> > nul, creates the shell at 0x4014b8 and resumes its thread at 0x4014d9. This follows the copy/registry operation in the selected mode.

Other retained branches extract resource type DLL/ID 101 using 0x402460, then write it through CreateFileA/WriteFile. 0x401150 creates a child, allocates remote memory, writes the DLL pathname and passes a resolved export to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d. This verifies the injection implementation beyond API co-occurrence.

The LoadLibraryA export is requested from a randomized module-name string at 0x404318; that normally cannot resolve Kernel32. The LanmanServer subkey string at 0x404340 and Active Setup strings at 0x4043fc/0x4043f0 are also replaced with random strings. Code retains the attack template but successful original persistence/injection is not claimed.

Embedded PE at 0x5060 has 39936 bytes, only 2200 nonzero; imports and almost all code are erased, including the entry region. HTTP/User-Agent/URLDownloadToFile strings in it do not prove working HTTP C2, payload downloading or DDoS.
The encoded fact is mechanical URL decoding of a damaged printf GUID template, not an encrypted endpoint. No Remcos, WannaCry encryption, ransom or credential-theft behavior was found.
samples.trait_decision: Existing hostile resource/injector identities and shell self-delete composite accurately describe retained code, with one suspicious resolved-export remote-DLL handoff. No successful deployment or intact embedded bot is asserted.

samples.identification: Custom NanoCoreFinal-labeled .NET surveillance and command implant, masquerading as Windows Update
samples.marker_line: Custom managed surveillance implant: fix dropper; add debugger gate
execution_evidence: CLR entry token 0x06000033 is Program.Main (RVA 0x2910). It invokes plugins, clipboard/screenshots/file targeting, reverse shell and command polling, then repeatedly reports a heartbeat. NanoCoreFinal and NanoCoreClientV1.2.0 are self-assigned labels; bytes do not establish stock NanoCore lineage.

KeyloggerModule.Start (RVA 0x20cc) installs hook ID 13. HookCallback (RVA 0x21dc) checks WM_KEYDOWN, reads the key code, appends timestamp/window-title/key records to a buffer, and SendLoop (RVA 0x22e8) writes keylog.txt and calls SendToC2 with Base64 key records. This is a surveillance implementation; hook delivery/message pumping and runtime success were not demonstrated.

SendToC2 (RVA 0x3c78) converts the input record to UTF8, XORs every byte with a repeating 32-byte key (index XOR 0xaa), Base64-encodes and URI-escapes it into a GET query, and calls HttpWebRequest.GetResponse. SendFile (RVA 0x37f0) supplies complete file bytes through this same reporting routine. Clipboard and screen loops supply captured content, and PasswordRecoveryModule reads Chromium Login Data/Cookies/History through SendFile. There is no browser password decryption.

StartCommandExecutor worker (RVA 0x3a24) reads the /cmd response into a string. Its download command sends a LOCAL existing file through SendFile; it does not download an HTTP payload. Other responses become cmd.exe /c arguments; captured stdout is reported as CMD_OUT. WriteAllBytes elsewhere writes a zero-filled placeholder DLL and random temporary files, not a downloaded executable.

The reverse-shell worker (RVA 0x38bc) connects a TcpClient and wraps its stream in a reader/writer; helpers RVA 0x3844/0x3880 relay received lines to child cmd stdin and cmd stdout to the network writer. This confirms paired stream coupling, not just socket and shell imports.

Config.C2_DOMAIN is http://wap-vebo.com, already including a scheme. Reporting and command routines prepend http:// again, and TcpClient uses that scheme-bearing string as a hostname. These malformed endpoints prevent the configured communication paths from working normally. Collection/backdoor code is retained; no successful theft or network contact was demonstrated.

Main writes HKCU Run entries pointing to its own executable and a self-copy, writes a startup batch launcher, creates a logon task, and attempts a BootExecute modification (whose String cast is incompatible with a normal multi-string value). It also writes the ms-settings shell command plus empty DelegateExecute before starting fodhelper. These are unwanted reactivation and elevation attempts, not normal updater work.

Main launches hidden PowerShell with Defender disabling arguments and net.exe with fixed-password account creation and Administrators membership arguments. It requests process class 29 with a true flag to make termination critical. Privilege checks and OS acceptance can prevent these effects.

Main IL +0x4ed..+0x50c resolves to IsDebuggerPresent OR Debugger.IsAttached followed by Environment.Exit(0). This actual conditional exit is missing from the initial objective findings and motivates the new suspicious detection.

The process-injection buffer is 31 c0 83 c0 64 c3 (xor eax,eax; add eax,100; ret). It is written into a notepad process and started with CreateRemoteThread; it is not process hollowing. TECHNIQUE:AMSI_Patch and TECHNIQUE:ETW_Patch only go to SendToC2; there are no corresponding patch effects.

Camera code attempts VFW driver-connect and SaveDIB message 1061 before reading/transmitting a saved BMP. Microphone code queries devices but launches an invalid AxHost-based recorder command, so no functional microphone recording is asserted. No new hostile traits were invented for these placeholders or failed paths.
There is no ConfuserEx metadata, decryptor or control-flow obfuscation. Ordinary CIL metadata exposes the methods and call graph; XOR is applied to outgoing records, not used to hide executable code.
samples.trait_decision: Remove the false ConfuserEx HTTP dropper finding and retain accurate keylogging, collection, command, reverse-shell, persistence, Defender-disable, masquerade and privilege-abuse findings. Add the independently verified debugger exit layout as suspicious; do not lower accurate severities to reach an arbitrary count.

verification.rescans: All three atomscan runs used --no-update --mode slow --follow=none and CLEAVE_TRAITS_DIR pointing at this checkout. Exit 1 reflects detection, not an analysis failure. The only deltas are removal of the unsupported HTTP dropper and addition of the suspicious debugger gate on the managed sample. Native outer/embedded findings remain unchanged.
verification.scope: No dependency packages were fetched or implicated. No sample was executed.
